inherited.M01: Two-stage training (frozen first stage plus second-stage mel refiner) and DiT/FastSpeech2 backbone inherited from prior flow-matching TTS and L2S post-training lineages.
inherited.M04: Silent talking-face/lip video as the only use-time input, inherited from the standard video-to-speech (lip-to-speech) lineage.
inherited.M05: Optical camera with 96x96 grayscale lip crops, dlib 68-landmark alignment, 16 kHz audio and 80-bin mel front end inherited from the CN-CVS visual-speech processing lineage.
inherited.M07: Speaker-embedding conditioning with no output LM, lexicon or beam search, inherited from the biosignal-to-speech voice-control lineage.
inherited.M08: HiFi-GAN neural vocoder turning refined mel spectrograms into waveform, inherited from the neural-vocoder L2S lineage.
inherited.M09: No presentation, confirmation or commit step; the absent interaction step is inherited from the one-shot video-to-speech synthesis lineage.
inherited.M10: No correction or re-entry step; the absence is inherited from the one-shot video-to-speech synthesis lineage.
inherited.M13: Offline two-4090 training and research-only CN-CVS Mandarin scope with dialects/accents deferred to future work, inherited from the standard academic L2S setup.

topics.inclusion_rule: Include studies that synthesize speech from a non-acoustic speech signal and train the signal encoder to predict self-supervised speech representations (HuBERT units, soft units, ContentVec, wav2vec features) derived from paired or aligned audio, instead of or besides spectral targets. Boundary: exclude recognition-only studies, targets the model generates itself, and acoustic-input conversion; count versions once.

Include lip-reading, visual speech recognition and video-to-speech studies whose ledger names a non-English target language (Mandarin, Chinese, German, Korean, Spanish and others) or a multilingual or cross-lingual setting, and classify from the full text (reference list removed) whether the visual encoder is pretrained on English or other external data and then transferred, is an AV-HuBERT-family encoder, or is trained from scratch. Boundary: a study counts under every design its text names (upper bound; related-work mentions included); audio-only encoders excluded; versions counted once.
topics.metric: CER/TER (character/tone error rate) of the target-language synthesis, lower is better

topics.inclusion_rule: Include the video-to-speech population of components/M06/video-to-speech-synthesis (speech waveform synthesized from talking-face or lip video, audio muted at test) and classify, from the full text with the reference list removed, how the acoustic decoder handles the one-to-many mapping: explicit pitch or energy (variance) predictors, flow-based decoders (normalizing flow, flow matching, rectified flow), diffusion decoders, adversarial training with a discriminator, and self-supervised speech-unit conditioning. Boundary: a study counts under every design its text names (upper bound; related-work mentions included); audio-visual enhancement with noisy audio at test, talking-head generation and video-to-text-to-TTS pipelines excluded; versions counted once.

topics.inclusion_rule: Include the video-to-speech population of components/M06 (speech waveform synthesized from talking-face or lip video, audio muted at test) and classify from the full text (reference list removed) how the text reference for ASR-scored intelligibility is built: ASR transcripts of the real audio used as the reference (re-transcription), and whether the ASR error on the real test audio is reported beside the systems. Boundary: a study counts under every design its text names (upper bound); audio-visual enhancement, talking-head generation and text-only lip reading excluded; versions counted once.

topics.metric: CER/TER (character/tone error rate) computed against ASR-retranscribed references, lower is better

topics.inclusion_rule: Include studies that synthesize a speech waveform from talking-face or lip video (the population of the M06 video-to-speech-synthesis table) and compare how the synthesized speech is evaluated: human listener or opinion tests, ASR word error on the synthesized speech, and tests on speakers unseen in training. Boundary: audio-visual enhancement with noisy audio at test, talking-head generation, text-only lip reading and video-to-text-to-TTS pipelines excluded; a study counts under every protocol its full text names (upper bound, related-work mentions included); versions counted once.
